angle: The deck the whole pod sees coming: a command-zone token swarm carrying a fully verified 2x2 matrix of zero-mana table-kills, whose real edge is redundancy — four corners, three tutors, and the learned skill of presenting the corner the table's open mana cannot answer.

THE LOOP SWORDS CAN'T STOP: Sanguine Bond + Exquisite Blood — no creature ever touches the stack

departments.headline: CAST EVERYTHING BUT HIM
departments.dek: What's the best card in a deck that starts every game with it face up and never pays a mana for it? Edgar Markov makes a Vampire for every Vampire you cast — from the command zone, from turn 1, for free — and thanks to four verified loops, the game that goes long is yours too.

callouts.title: BANK BODIES
callouts.text: Turns 1-3: deploy down the 8/18/18 curve of one-, two-, and three-drop Vampires. Every cast is two bodies — the creature and the eminence token — and the payoffs find themselves: a lord or Vampire payoff is drawn by turn 6 in 66.3% of simulated games. Do not cast Edgar. The engine costs nothing while he sits at home.

callouts.title: LAYER THE ENGINES
callouts.text: Turns 4-6: add what makes width lethal against three life totals — a drain engine (drawn by turn 6 in 62.7% of games), a token doubler (42.2%), and the aristocrats layer: Viscera Seer, Cruel Celebrant, and Grave Pact turn every spare token into a scry, a table-wide drain, and an edict. Deploy under wrath-math — commit what wins, no further — knowing a sweep costs the table almost as much as it costs you.

callouts.title: PICK YOUR KILL — YOU HAVE TWO
callouts.text: Turn 6 and later, take whichever window opens first. The attack turn: cast Edgar (median turn 6) into a protected seven-wide swing — 14 from every opponent at declare (stack 003), another 14 at your end step (stack 007, verified reach, not a kill), counters from Edgar's own trigger on top. Or the stack: tutor the missing half of the 2x2 loop matrix — and when the table holds open mana, fetch toward Sanguine Bond plus Exquisite Blood, the pairing instant-speed creature removal cannot break.

captions.Edgar Markov: **THE ENGINE:** eminence makes a 1/1 Vampire per other Vampire spell you cast — while he is in the command zone. The deck's core engine is online before your first land drop, and no removal spell in the format can touch it.
captions.Sanguine Bond: **THE SECOND LOSE-HALF:** Vito's trigger, word for word, on an enchantment — the card that makes the kill a 2x2 matrix instead of a single column.
captions.Viscera Seer: **THE CONVERTER:** one mana, instant-speed sacrifices, a scry per body — the card that makes every free eminence token worth something on its way out too.

pilot_tips.text: Never cast Edgar just because you hit six mana — cast him the turn you intend to swing wide with protection held, because his engine runs at full power from the zone and his body is the pivot, not the plan.

departments.pull_quote: The engine costs zero. The long game belongs to you too.

departments.headline: NEVER KEEP FOR EDGAR
departments.dek: He's face up in the command zone before your first decision, so the drill is pure engine-hand arithmetic: enablers over payoffs, untapped over tapped. The Coach grades four real hands; Ledger prints the rate — 81.7% of first sevens keep, at 0.219 mulligans a game.

hands.why: Three lands that can all enter untapped, two one-mana Vampires (each worth two bodies), a lord, and a refill. This is the enabler-heavy shape that wins the engine-hand test — the payoffs find themselves: a lord or payoff is drawn by turn 6 in 66.3% of games.

Two lands reads risky until you price the mana: Tomb into Ring is four mana on turn 1, and Herald's Horn discounts every body behind it while digging at each upkeep. The nuance that saves this keep — 16 of the 37 lands can enter tapped, so a two-land hand needs its lands untapped. These are.

cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
hands.why: Three loop halves in one opener feels like destiny — and it is the classic all-payoff mulligan: no play before turn 3, the entire eminence dividend skipped, and your kill telegraphed from the first discard. The tutors are the real copies. Enablers are what an opener must actually hold.

hands.verdict: SHIP — the flood the sim would keep
hands.why: The goldfish's mechanical rule keeps 2-5 lands, so this five-lander passes the machine — and the Coach overrules it. One spell to cast before turn 4, and protection plus a tutor are luxuries in an opener, not a plan. The badge difference, printed honestly: the diamond says keepable, the star says ship.

captions.Concealed Courtyard: **THE FIRST-THREE-TURNS LAND:** untapped exactly through the land drops when an 8-one-drop, 18-two-drop curve needs it most.

pilot_tips.text: Grade one-drops on casts, not stats — Viscera Seer on turn 1 is a body, a banked eminence token, and a machine that will out-value most rares in this deck by turn 8.

departments.pull_quote: He lives in the command zone. Mulligan like he doesn't exist.

departments.headline: PIVOT OR PATIENCE
departments.dek: One board asks whether six mana is Edgar or two more Vampires; the other asks what a tutor is really for when the whole table knows what you'd fetch. Commit out loud — then, and only then, read the Coach's call.

callouts.title: HOW TO PLAY ALONG
callouts.text: Cover the recommendation box. Read the board, pick a branch, say it out loud — the signals and coalition risks are printed with each branch so you can argue with them. Being wrong on this page is free; being wrong at the table costs a game.

callouts.title: TURN 6: THE ALPHA WINDOW
callouts.text: Decision 001. Six mana, four banked tokens, a draw-go player with four untapped lands, an aggro seat at 12 and tapped out. Edgar now, a bigger board, or a smaller board with protection held? Every branch is defensible. One is right.

callouts.title: TURN 8: THE HIDDEN HALF
callouts.text: Decision 002. Vito survived a full table rotation, Demonic Tutor in hand, eight lands untapped — and the control seat has held five mana all game. Fetch and present, fetch and hide, or hold the tutor as an answer? Four verified corners say the kill is real; the question is whether this is its window.

captions.Swiftfoot Boots: **THE QUIET ENABLER:** hexproof plus haste for one to equip is the difference between an Edgar who pivots the game and an Edgar who eats the removal the table saved six turns for.

pilot_tips.text: Ask which wrath you actually fear before leaning on Flawless Maneuver — indestructible beats destroy effects, and does nothing against Toxic Deluge's -X/-X or an exile sweeper.

departments.pull_quote: An assumption is not a target.

departments.headline: ARCHENEMY, IN WRITING
departments.dek: Eminence banks a visible body from turn 1, and your 99 holds the four most famous drain pairings in the format. When your threat level is structural, deflection buys turns, not phases — so spend them on purpose.

callouts.title: THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: The board state that flips you to archenemy: any visible loop half next to open black mana. The strategic frame is blunt — with roughly 355,000 combined combo-database entries across your four pairings, the deflection budget is largely pre-spent by seat assignment. Deflection buys single turns. Spend those turns on purpose.

callouts.title: THE OPEN SECRET
callouts.text: At a bracket-4 floor, sandbagging four famous combos reads as bad faith, not cleverness — play the kill-web honestly as a co-equal plan. Honesty is not surrender: declare the deck, then make the table solve the sequencing. A lone Exquisite Blood or Bloodthirsty Conqueror still reads as value and passively feeds on all table damage; the moment a second complementary half is visible, you are the archenemy on the clock.

callouts.title: SEQUENCE BY REMOVAL WINDOW
callouts.text: The real concealment is which corner you present. Your tutors put the missing half where no removal reaches — hand and library — so fetch toward the pairing the table's open mana cannot answer: against held creature removal, Sanguine Bond plus Exquisite Blood (stack 005, no creature in the loop); the creature corners only when the answer-holders are tapped out. Complete the pair in the dead window, never into it.

captions.Demonic Tutor: **THE ARMOR:** the table knows what a tutor with a loop half on board means — but an assumption is not a target, and a card in hand cannot be Dispatched.
captions.Grave Pact: **THE RESENTMENT ENGINE:** every token death forces each opponent to sacrifice — and Viscera Seer supplies those deaths on demand. Value that makes enemies; fire it while your deflection budget still has a balance.
captions.Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet: **THE QUIET GRUDGE:** exiling everything the table's creatures do when they die — and minting you Zombies for it — is the kind of card opponents remember. He anchors your defense; expect him to draw the removal your loop halves didn't.

pilot_tips.text: Cast Exquisite Blood while it still reads as a lifegain trinket — alone it draws no removal, it feeds on every point of damage anywhere at the table, and once it's down only the cheap half of two different loops is ever exposed again.

departments.pull_quote: You cannot sandbag four famous combos. Wear the label — and make the table answer the right corner.

departments.headline: WHO DRAINS THE DRAINER
departments.dek: A single 'players can't gain life' effect switches off all four loops at once — and never touches the drains. Name the layer of your deck that survives each nightmare below, before you sit down to it.

threats.read: The wrath costs them more than it costs you. Grave Pact and Cruel Celebrant convert the board they sweep into edicts and each-opponent drains, Viscera Seer cashes tokens at instant speed in response, the two enchantment halves and an indestructible (and usually noncreature) Purphoros survive outright, and eminence rebuilds at one token per cast with no recast tax — Bloodghast for free on a land drop. Commit only what wins before the sweep, and do not fear the long game: four verified corners are inevitability. The one unrebuildable loss is Edgar himself — the next cast is 8.

Know exactly which layer dies: 'players can't gain life' turns off the ENTIRE 2x2 matrix — every corner needs a gain-half to fire — and blanks the lifelink bodies. But your hate-proof plan is verified three ways: Sanctum Seeker's each-opponent trigger doubled by Bloodletter is life LOSS (stack 003's 14 at declare), Throne's end-step echo is life loss (stack 007's 14 — reach, not a kill), and Purphoros deals damage with no lifegain anywhere in sight (stack 008's 10 per cast). Stop tutoring for gain-halves; start tutoring for the hate's answer — or for Purphoros, who never noticed the hate was there.

You are the forced beatdown: the 18-and-18 two/three-drop core is exactly the many-cheap-spells profile that Sphere effects halve, and your mana is already taxed — 16 of 37 lands enter tapped and mean available mana is 5.344 on turn 6. Race the lock's assembly and aim removal at the one piece that beats YOU (usually the per-cast tax, since eminence pays per cast). Two hedges: Herald's Horn rebates one generic mana on nearly every spell you cast, and the loops are notably tax-resistant once assembled — every corner needs zero mana to iterate. Edgar stays zoned longest here.

Answer economy inverts: the last profitable moment for held interaction is now. Your counter-clock is fast — four corners, three tutors, and 5.4%-by-turn-6 natural assembly mean the tutored kill is usually one turn away once either half sticks. The white removal and Deflecting Swat protect that turn, with the standing tension that Swat is free only once Edgar resolves — a real argument for an earlier, unprotected Edgar against a known combo seat. Present the kill first, and prefer presenting the all-enchantment corner.

pilot_tips.text: Feed Bloodghast to Viscera Seer, Diabolic Intent, and Grave Pact without hesitation — it can't block anyway, and it returns on any land drop, fetch cracks included.
Cast Olivia's Wrath as an attack, not a rescue — with a wide Vampire board its -X/-X clears every blocker and misses your entire army.

departments.pull_quote: Life loss isn't lifegain — the hate card silences four loops and leaves the declare-step drain, the end-step echo, and the god untouched.
departments.note: Four boxes as listed; the lifegain-hate box is the department's teaching peak, because the matrix makes the hate card table-correct. Against creature aggro the honest note stands: the control seat is held with drains, edicts, and Kalitas rather than blockers — Vampire of the Dire Moon is the deck's only one-drop deathtouch defender.

departments.headline: THREE TUTORS, FOUR HALVES
departments.dek: Natural loop assembly is 5.4% by turn 6 — the tutors ARE the assembly, and each one is a copy of whichever half you're missing. One wish per tutor. Here's how not to waste it.

captions.Diabolic Intent: **DEMONIC TUTOR, TOKEN-PRICED:** the additional cost is a creature, and eminence prints the currency — a sacrifice that also pays out under Cruel Celebrant, Cordial Vampire, and Grave Pact on its way to the bin.

pilot_tips.text: Cast Vampiric Tutor at the end step of the player before you — the card lands on your next draw, the table sees one mana spent, and nobody learns what you went and got.

departments.pull_quote: Fetch the half the table's open mana cannot answer.

departments.headline: THE ZONE IS THE ENGINE
departments.dek: The command zone usually promises guaranteed access to a card you still have to cast. Eminence works from the zone itself — so what, exactly, is the table supposed to remove?
departments.body:
Exhibit one, the guarantee, inverted. An eminence ability states its zones and functions from them — the command zone included (CR 113.6b) — so this deck's engine is not merely guaranteed access, it is guaranteed operation. No mulligan needs to find it, because no hand carries it. No removal answers it, because no permanent hosts it. The Counselor's holding: from turn 1, every other Vampire spell you cast is two bodies, and the record shows no legal objection.

Exhibit two, the tax ladder. A commander costs an additional {2} for each previous cast from the command zone (CR 903.8): {3}{R}{W}{B} the first time, 8 the second, 10 the third. Set the ladder beside the deck's own means — 5.344 mana available on turn 6, per the simulation — and each rung prices itself. The wrinkle unique to this deck: recasting is genuinely optional. A dead Edgar keeps making tokens from the zone; the tax buys back only the alpha-strike trigger and the free-protection condition. Pay it for a kill, never for company.

Exhibit three, colour identity. Your commander's colour identity governs every card in the deck, lands and rules text included (CR 903.4). Mardu buys this deck white protection and exile, black tutors and drains, and red's per-cast burn; it permanently locks out counterspells and green ramp — which is why the manabase works as hard as Sources Say documents. The box observes the same law: Runo Stromkirk's blue identity makes it unplayable under Edgar, and it stays a collection card.

Exhibit four, the clock. A player dealt 21 or more combat damage by the same commander loses (CR 903.10a). Here the 21 is a coincidence, not a plan — Edgar swings as one attacker among seven, and the deck's real clocks are the each-opponent drains, the per-cast burn, and four zero-mana loops. Know the rule; expect to win by the other ledgers.

Now the Coach takes the pen. The political read: the table sees Edgar in the zone and prices the whole engine from seat assignment — you do not get a quiet game, so stop paying for one. And the protect-versus-race call has an eminence twist: Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat are free only while you control a commander, which the zone plan delays until the pivot. So the insurance and the alpha strike arrive on the same turn, by design. Before it, protection costs the exact mana the curve wants for Vampires. Budget accordingly, and cast Edgar the turn he converts the board — not a turn sooner.

captions.Flawless Maneuver: **PRICED IN EDGAR:** free only while you control a commander. The eminence plan keeps him zoned until the pivot, so this reads {2}{W} for the first five turns — the deck's central protection tension.

pilot_tips.text: Count Deflecting Swat as part of Edgar's casting-cost math — the turn he resolves, it flips from a three-mana trick to free interaction, which is a real argument for an earlier Edgar against a known combo seat.

departments.pull_quote: Removal cannot touch the command zone. The table's only answer to eminence is to end the game.

departments.headline: EVERY CAST COUNTS TWICE
departments.dek: Sixty-three spells with a hidden common cost: each Vampire cast also prints a body from the command zone. The kill matrix and its couriers lead, the aristocrats convert, and a manabase hauling 50 black pips closes.

captions.Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth: **THE PATCH:** every land becomes a Swamp under a manabase owing 50 black pips across 36 black cards — your painlands and white sources all pay the tribe's real bill.
captions.Welcoming Vampire: **THE STEADY REFILL:** a card per turn whenever another power-2-or-less creature enters — every eminence token switches it on.

pilot_tips.text: Pay Rite of Oblivion's sacrifice with an eminence token — a nearly-free exile that flashes back for a second one later.

departments.pull_quote: Twenty-nine threats, one sweeper of your own, and an engine no wrath can reach.
departments.note: Rank matters: the matrix leads because it is why the bracket floor reads 4; mana closes. Full card blurbs render from manual_prose.card_roles; the remaining lands render in the Depth group. The 34-card box renders as its own labeled strip, pointing to The Short List for the rulings. Print the honesty note: 12 maindeck cards — including Sanguine Bond, Exquisite Blood, Grave Pact, and Anointed Procession — have no role-taxonomy entry; absence of a role chip is a limit of the taxonomy, not of the card. No synergy-graph claim appears anywhere in the issue (1 intra-deck edge; it is a global shortlist, not a fit score).

departments.headline: TEN FOR THE SLEEVES
departments.dek: Eight from the box, two scouted from the wider pool — and the headline is a third lose-half that would turn the verified 2x2 into a 2x3. I print the counts and the ranks; the lines a card would open stay candidates until a stack passes.

callouts.title: THE SCOUT: MARAUDING BLIGHT-PRIEST
callouts.text: An in-tribe three-drop whose text — 'whenever you gain life, each opponent loses 1 life' — pairs with both sleeved gain-halves. Two new pairings on the combo graph, each drains every opponent with no per-iteration retargeting, and the card banks an eminence token on the way in. The count that matters: both lines still need a stack scenario. Until one passes, this is the best candidate in the pool, not a fifth corner.

callouts.title: THE SCOUT: BLOODCHIEF ASCENSION
callouts.text: One mana against the obsolescence index's read on Sanguine Bond's shape, EDHREC rank 742 — the best-ranked candidate anywhere in this analysis. The intuition behind the numbers: stack 003's verified 14-per-opponent attack turn charges all three quest counters in a single combat, after which every card hitting any graveyard drains 2 and gains 2. The bound, printed: the index's hit is CMC-based; three counters must land first.

callouts.title: THE PURCHASE IS REDUNDANCY
callouts.text: Read the ten as one purchase made ten ways. A singleton format prices consistency two ways — more copies of the job, or tutors that fetch it — and this deck already runs the tutors. So the list buys copies: a third lose-half, a second and third sac outlet behind Viscera Seer, the box's only repeatable draw engine, and a deathtouch wall for the fair fights. Every bracket delta computes 4-to-4. The floor never moves; the frequency of reaching it does.

captions.Elenda, the Dusk Rose: **THE HELD PAYOFF:** a counter from every death anywhere, then a doubled army of lifelink tokens on her way out — in the box until the maindeck death engine proves it feeds her.
captions.Gifted Aetherborn: **THE WALL IN WAITING:** two mana, deathtouch, lifelink — the box's answer for aggressive pods, where the 99's only one-drop deathtouch defender needs company.

pilot_tips.text: Watch Voldaren Pariah's seat — it is the named natural cut if Marauding Blight-Priest's two loop lines ever pass a stack scenario, so let that file run before you re-sleeve anything.

departments.pull_quote: Redundancy is one purchase, made ten ways.

departments.headline: PAY BLACK FIRST
departments.dek: Black is 64.9% of this deck's pips on a 41.5% source share: 22 black land sources, on curve 63.9% of the time where white sits at 83.1%. The audit prices that gap — the fix is sequencing, not shame.

captions.Mana Confluence: **THE BEST FIXING IN THE DECK:** any colour at 1 life per tap — priced in the one resource the drain suite replenishes by the dozen.

pilot_tips.text: Play Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth the turn a double-black cast is stuck in hand — every land you control taps for the exact colour the audit flags.

departments.pull_quote: White and red take care of themselves. Black never does — pay it first.
departments.note: The tables, meters, and stated-assumptions box render from mana_analysis.json; the body prose from the writer's mana_base key. The 90% yardstick is a yardstick: the artifact's own note says 36 black sources is not a possibility in a 37-land deck, and Ledger's copy prices what the gap costs (black on curve 63.9% lands-only, 71.8% with rocks) instead of grading it.

departments.headline: THE BODY COUNT
departments.dek: Ten thousand seeded runs, no opponents, no mercy. What a zero-mana engine actually produces, why a six-drop commander still waits until turn 6 — and the honest 5.4% behind the kill matrix.

callouts.title: BODIES WITHOUT A COMMANDER
callouts.text: Mean bodies: 1.69 by turn 3, 4.04 by turn 6, 6.343 by turn 10 — with zero mana ever spent on Edgar. That is the eminence dividend, and the model doesn't even count doubler multiplication beyond parsed token text.

callouts.title: MEDIAN CAST: TURN 6
callouts.text: Edgar lands by turn 6 in 51.2% of runs (mean 6.628). The histogram's spike is turn 6 at 3,764 of 10,000, and 1,656 runs never cast him by turn 10 — losing nothing but the alpha strike for it. A commander you never have to cast is the cheapest six-drop in the format.

callouts.title: THE 5.4% MATRIX
callouts.text: A loop pair — any lose-half plus any gain-half — assembles naturally in 5.4% of runs by turn 6 and 9.4% by turn 10. Four halves make every draw step live, but read the number honestly: those two figures exclude the three tutors, so they are a floor. Let a drawn, affordable tutor fetch one missing half and assembly runs 19.1% by turn 6 and 30.9% by turn 10.

callouts.title: THE TAPPED-LAND TAX
callouts.text: 16 of 37 lands can enter tapped; land drops fall to 58.2% by turn 6 and mean available mana is 5.344 — which is the whole story of why a six-mana commander waits. The curve lives at one, two, and three on purpose, and Herald's Horn's rebate (ramp-or-fixing drawn: 50.2% by turn 6) eases the squeeze.

captions.Herald's Horn: **LAB NOTE:** cost reducers and rituals are not modeled, and the assembly figures quoted here exclude tutors — every figure on this page is the floor. The real deck casts more, drains more, and completes the matrix more often than the chart admits.

pilot_tips.text: Lead Ancient Tomb into a two-drop Vampire whenever the opener offers it — two colourless on turn 1 is a body plus a banked eminence token before anyone else has moved.

departments.pull_quote: Half the runs cast Edgar by turn 6. Every run works his engine from turn 1.
departments.note: The stated-assumptions box is non-negotiable: the model simulates resource development, not games, and reports pair assembly two ways — 5.4%/9.4% is the tutor-free figure, 19.1%/30.9% the tutor-assisted one beside it. Cite every figure exactly as goldfish_metrics.json reports: 0.512, 6.628, median 6, 1.69, 4.04, 6.343, 0.582, 5.344, 0.054, 0.094, 0.191, 0.309, 0.663, 0.627, 0.575, 0.506, 0.502, 0.422, 0.817, 0.219, histogram 3764, not_by_max_turn 1656. Seed 42, 10,000 iterations.

departments.headline: EIGHT FILES, THREE MOVEMENTS
departments.dek: An overture, a matrix, and an attack turn scored twice — every file argued against the June 19, 2026 comprehensive rules and affirmed by the checker, including the one that came back stamped 'not a table-kill.' The Counselor prints that one just as large.

callouts.title: OVERTURE: FIVE BODIES, TWO MANA
callouts.text: Stack 002, the everyday engine: a two-mana Vampire cast with Edgar zoned and both doublers out. Eminence triggers once, Anointed Procession and Mondrak, Glory Dominus double the same token event in either order — 1 becomes 2 becomes 4, and the checker confirmed order does not matter — and all four tokens enter with Vampire Socialite counters. Five new bodies, one cast; tokens are created, not cast, so eminence never re-triggers on them. Every other file on these pages runs on this arithmetic. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-002.

callouts.title: THE MATRIX: 38 TRIGGERS
callouts.text: Stack 001, the marquee corner: Exquisite Blood plus Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose, seeded by an ordinary 2-point lifelink hit. Each Vito trigger is a new object targeted fresh, so you walk the drain across the table — 6, 13, and 19 resolutions clear opponents at 12, 25, and 38 life, 38 iterations total, and a mid-loop death never breaks the chain, because the killing loss still triggers your enchantment. You end at 105 life having spent nothing. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-001.

callouts.title: THE MATRIX: THE UNTOUCHABLE CORNER
callouts.text: Stack 005: Sanguine Bond plus Exquisite Blood — both enchantments. From a 2-life seed, 26 Bond resolutions clear the table (9, then 17), the chain crosses the first opponent's death, and you win by rule 104.2a at 79 life. This is the corner to tutor toward when the table holds open mana: no creature sits anywhere in the loop, so the per-iteration removal window the other corners must confess to simply does not exist. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-005.

callouts.title: THE MATRIX: THE FRAGILE TWIN
callouts.text: Stack 004: Bloodthirsty Conqueror's trigger matches Exquisite Blood's word for word — the checker confirmed '(Damage causes loss of life.)' is reminder text, not a requirement — and 13 iterations from a 3-life seed killed a 9- and a 30-life opponent with zero overkill. The honest cost at full size: the gain-half is a 5/5 creature, so every iteration's priority window admits instant-speed removal. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-004.

callouts.title: THE MATRIX: CLOSING THE SQUARE
callouts.text: Stack 006: Sanguine Bond plus Bloodthirsty Conqueror, 13 Bond resolutions from a 3-life seed — 4, then 9, each overkilling by exactly 1, because 3 divides neither total. One creature half means one removal target per iteration: fewer than 004's pairing, more than 005's zero. Four corners, four stamps — whichever half the tutor finds first, you already know what completes it. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-006.

callouts.title: ATTACK TURN, PART ONE: FOURTEEN AT DECLARE
callouts.text: Stack 003, the fair kill: seven Vampires attack with Sanctum Seeker and Bloodletter of Aclazotz among them. Seven Seeker triggers, each opponent's loss doubled on your turn: 14 from every opponent at declare attackers, before a single blocker is named — and the checker confirmed the opponent at 14 hits exactly 0 and is eliminated by state-based actions mid-combat. Your gain is 7, never doubled: Bloodletter reads opponents only. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-003.

callouts.title: ATTACK TURN, PART TWO: THE ECHO THAT ISN'T A KILL
callouts.text: Stack 007, the honest file: the same seven attackers, now tapped, plus Throne of the God-Pharaoh. At your end step each opponent loses 7 — doubled by Bloodletter to 14, who stayed home untapped and so does not count itself. Verified — and PARTIALLY REFUTED as a table-kill, in the artifact's own words: a 15-life opponent survives at exactly 1. The 28-per-opponent full-turn figure is arithmetic composed from two separately verified files, not one checker-passed line. Present it as reach, never as lethal-by-default. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-007.

callouts.title: ATTACK TURN, PART THREE: TEN PER HEAD, PER CAST
callouts.text: Stack 008: with Purphoros, God of the Forge and both doublers out, one two-mana Vampire cast is four simultaneous token entries — four separate Purphoros triggers, the checker confirmed — plus a fifth when the spell's own body arrives. Five triggers, 2 damage each, to every opponent: 10 per head per cast, no combat required, and the verified line's opponent at 10 hit exactly 0 on the fifth resolution. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-008.

captions.Sanguine Bond: **LOSE-HALF, NO BODY:** Vito's trigger on an enchantment Swords can't reach — verified with both gain-halves (stacks 005 and 006), and the key to the matrix's only creature-free corner.
captions.Bloodthirsty Conqueror: **GAIN-HALF, HONEST COST:** the same words on a 5/5 flying deathtouch body — a removal window every iteration, and a fair-game monster the loop never needs.
captions.Purphoros, God of the Forge: **THE CAST TAX:** 10 to every opponent per two-mana Vampire through both doublers — indestructible, and usually not a creature, so the wrath your tokens invite doesn't touch him.

pilot_tips.text: Never wait for a big lifegain event to start a loop — stacks 001 and 005 were both seeded by an ordinary 2-point lifelink connect, and any lifelink body in the 99 can supply it.

departments.pull_quote: Four loops, one table — and the resilient corner never puts a creature on the stack.
departments.note: The issue's peak: stage it as three movements, not eight equal spreads. Movement one (A-002) is the overture at feature scale. Movement two is the centerpiece: a literal 2x2 grid spread — rows are lose-halves (Vito, Sanguine Bond), columns are gain-halves (Exquisite Blood, Bloodthirsty Conqueror) — with kill counts 38/13/26/13 printed in each cell, callouts n2-n5 anchoring the corners, and per-corner removal-window glyphs teaching the sequencing skill. Movement three (A-003, A-007, A-008) walks one attack turn chronologically: declare, end step, and the casts that built it. The pull quote runs full-width between movements two and three as the lung; 007's refutation panel is the honesty beat, printed at the same size as the wins. Map-key carries the life glyph and a token glyph. Copy discipline: the department's own copy says 'a 2-point lifelink hit' and 'a two-mana Vampire' — the math is card-agnostic; the artifacts name their own staging cards and Judge's Desk prints them verbatim.

departments.headline: EIGHT FILES, EIGHT STAMPS
departments.dek: Bad blood, good paperwork: every citation verbatim, every verdict as issued. One file needed a second attempt, and one is stamped 'not a table-kill' — the Counselor tells you which, because that is the entire point of this desk.
departments.note: Renderer-generated from the eight checker-passed artifacts; nothing summarized, truncated, or paraphrased. Case order A-001 through A-008 with verdict and iteration count as case status — A-003 passed on iteration 2 (the near-miss is credibility, not embarrassment); all others passed on iteration 1. A-007's status line must carry its own artifact's language: verified as a 14-per-opponent end-step drain, PARTIALLY REFUTED as a table-kill. One-line staging note where it applies: two files cast Gifted Aetherborn and two seed with Vampire Nighthawk's lifelink — cards that live in this deck's box rather than its 99; the findings are card-agnostic (any two-mana Vampire, any 2-point lifelink hit) and the files print as recorded. Manila, stamps, typewriter face throughout.

departments.headline: NINETY-THREE HANDS
departments.dek: Ninety-three artists split 131 cards, and the leaders hold four apiece — no standout, and that IS the finding. So the feature goes where the deck's own plot points: Volkan Baǵa, who painted the commander and the drain he leads into battle.

featured.note:
Two entries of 131 — no inflation, and both load-bearing: Edgar Markov himself, and Sanctum Seeker, the trigger that turns seven attackers into 14 life from every opponent at declare (stack 003). In a book where ninety-three hands split the work and nobody dominates, the closest thing to a house style is this coincidence: the artist who painted the face of the deck also painted its favourite attack.

The wider census is the real story, and it reads as breadth, not curation: the collection was assembled card by card across a decade of printings — fifty-nine sets contribute, the largest gives fifteen cards by fifteen different artists, and the analysis found no contiguous collector-number runs. Nobody bought this deck whole. The numbers say so, and we print them that way.

also_worth_noting.note: Co-leader at four entries, all in the 99: Castle Locthwain, Luxury Suite, Savai Triome — the manabase's house painter — plus Throne of the God-Pharaoh, the verified end-step echo of stack 007.
The other co-leader at four: Arcane Signet and Diabolic Intent in the 99, Akroma's Memorial and Leering Onlooker in the box. Two shelves, one hand.
Three entries, one of them Mondrak, Glory Dominus — the doubler that sits inside two verified files (stacks 002 and 008).
Three entries, all in the 99, all nocturnes — Blood Crypt, Silent Clearing, Twilight Prophet. The deck's mood board in three frames.

captions.Sanctum Seeker: **SAME HAND AS THE BOSS:** Baǵa's other card is the attack-turn engine — each attacking Vampire drains every opponent for 1, and stack 003 verified what seven of them do under Bloodletter of Aclazotz.

departments.pull_quote: We count the cards, not the copies — four Swamps are one credit.
departments.note: The analysis reports no standout (lead artists hold 4 entries; its own note says tell a breadth story) and an empty drop-run list, so no bought-whole caveat applies — the featured pick is editorial, chosen for the story, with counts recomputed by the renderer. Scope note for the Art File box, printed: the census covers the pilot's full collection — the 99 plus the 34-card box, 131 entries and 136 copies across 93 artists. Respect the per-entry notes verbatim: Swamp is 1 entry/4 copies (per-copy would inflate Dimitar Marinski); Unholy Officiant and Vampire Nocturnus are 1 entry/2 copies each. rhythm_notes: The five acts carry the tempo. Act I rises from narrative (The Game Plan) through practice (Keep or Ship) to the participatory high of What's Your Play?; Act II holds the middle register — reflection, reference, instruction — with the threat boxes as its densest moment; Act III cools into browsing (The 99) and imagination (The Short List) before the climb; Act IV is the ascent: Sources Say and By the Numbers are the issue's only adjacent dense spreads, separated by the declared full-bleed art break the renderer emits after Sources Say, and The Kill is the late peak — staged as three movements (overture, matrix, attack turn) with the full-width pull quote as the lung between movements two and three and stack 007's refutation panel as the honesty beat before 008 closes. Act V tapers: the Desk is opt-in reference buffered by The Kill's narrative before it and Featured Artist's appreciation after, and the back page closes the loop. Pun budget, all in furniture and stopping at three: 'THE BODY COUNT' (a data headline literal enough to earn its keep), 'Bad blood, good paperwork' (the Desk's dek), and 'GO GET IT' against Fetch Quests' wish framing.
gaps: Two candidate lines remain unverified and are flagged, never asserted: Grave Pact's edict into Kalitas's exile replacement, and the Cruel Celebrant ignition ordering (a death seeding an assembled pair). One resolve-stack run each settles them.
Marauding Blight-Priest's two combo-graph pairings need stack scenarios before any 2x3 language hardens — The Short List prints them as candidates, status 'needs a stack scenario'.

The 5.4%/9.4% pair-assembly figures exclude tutors by construction; the tutor-assisted 19.1%/30.9% beside them models one drawn, affordable tutor fetching a missing half. The spread between the two is what the co-equal-plan framing should be grounded on wherever assembly is quoted.
